no_gates_linked.title: No gates linked to this number
no_gates_linked.description:
You're signed in, but no gates are linked to this phone number yet.

Open the **MyCentsys Remote** app and check that your gate appears there for this number. If it doesn't, the gate's admin needs to add your number as a **remote user** on the operator - a direct or Bluetooth-only connection isn't enough.

Once it's linked the gate appears here automatically within about a minute, and this notice clears itself. No restart needed.

**Community or shared gate?** Gates *shared* with your number (a community/estate site with actions like *Main Gate* or *Pedestrian Gate*) now appear here automatically too. If one isn't showing, check in the app that it's still shared to **this exact number** - and that you picked the **same country** here as in the app, since the wrong country changes the number.

shared_smart_readonly.title: Shared Wi-Fi gate is view-only
shared_smart_readonly.description:
A **Wi-Fi (SMART)** gate has been shared with your number, so Home Assistant shows its access details (when it expires, triggers left) - but it **can't open it**.

Unlike a gate you own, a *shared* Wi-Fi gate is opened by the MyCentsys app over **Bluetooth while you're standing at the gate**; there's no remote way to trigger it, from Home Assistant or from the app when you're away. This is how Centurion shares Wi-Fi gates, not something you can change here.

(If it's actually *your own* gate, add the integration again using the **owning** number instead - it'll then be fully controllable. Cellular **GSM/ULTRA** shared gates *are* controllable and aren't affected by this.)
